quote: Many resort to prayer only when in trouble. Such a practice is thoughtless and misleading.
True, you do well to pray when harassed, but you should also be mindful to speak as a son to your Father even when all goes well with your soul.
There is but one form of prayer which is appropriate for all God’s children, and that is: “Nevertheless, your will be done.”
in the human life of Jesus faith was personal, living, original, spontaneous, and purely spiritual.
Belief has attained the level of faith when it motivates life and shapes the mode of living.
Belief is always limiting and binding; faith is expanding and releasing. Belief fixates, faith liberates.
By faith you are justified; by faith are you saved; and by this same faith are you eternally advanced in the way of progressive and divine perfection.
Jesus loves men so much that his love awakens the response of love in the human heart. Love is truly contagious and eternally creative.
All true love is from God, and man receives the divine affection as he himself bestows this love upon his fellows.
It is not so important to love all men today as it is that each day you learn to love one more human being.
Love is never self-seeking, and it cannot be self-bestowed. Divine love cannot be self-contained; it must be unselfishly bestowed.
God is love, but love is not God.
Service—purposeful service, not slavery—is productive of the highest satisfaction and is expressive of the divinest dignity.
Service—more service, increased service, difficult service, adventurous service, and at last divine and perfect service—is the goal of time and the destination of space.
The privilege of service immediately follows the discovery of trustworthiness.
His courage was magnificent, but he was never foolhardy.
It was courage born of faith, not the recklessness of blind presumption.

The courage of the flesh is the lowest form of bravery. Mind bravery is a higher type of human courage, but the highest and supreme is uncompromising loyalty to the enlightened convictions of profound spiritual realities.
And such courage constitutes the heroism of the God-knowing man.
Worship is for its own sake; prayer embodies a self- or creature-interest element; that is the great difference between worship and prayer.
Worship asks nothing and expects nothing for the worshiper.
Worship is the highest joy of Paradise existence; it is the refreshing play of Paradise.
Regarding sin, he taught that God has forgiven; that we make such forgiveness personally available by the act of forgiving our fellows.
When you forgive your brother in the flesh, you thereby create the capacity in your own soul for the reception of the reality of God’s forgiveness of your own misdeeds.
And when you love your brother, you have already forgiven him.
Divine love does not merely forgive wrongs; it absorbs and actually destroys them.
Wisdom is twofold in origin, being derived from the perfection of divine insight inherent in perfect beings and from the personal experience acquired by evolutionary creatures.
In time, thinking leads to wisdom and wisdom leads to worship; in eternity, worship leads to wisdom, and wisdom eventuates in the finality of thought.
The peace of Jesus is the joy and satisfaction of a God-knowing individual who has achieved the triumph of learning fully how to do the will of God while living the mortal life in the flesh.

Personal peace integrates personality. Social peace prevents fear, greed, and anger. Political peace prevents race antagonisms, national suspicions, and war. Peacemaking is the cure of distrust and suspicion.
“My peace I leave with you.” “Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.”
Happiness and joy take origin in the inner life.
You cannot experience real joy all by yourself.
“The kingdom of God is not meat and drink but righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.”
